_note: Points that published register maps carry and the 394-field canonical registry has no field for. An unresolved tag NOT in this list is a defect: a simulator invented a spelling or a pack lost a row. Generated by energy-sprint/packs/build_gaps.py.

alternate_voltage_reference.reason: Line-to-neutral and line-to-line are different quantities on the same device — 277 V and 480 V on one wye meter — and the registry has a single voltage field. Each pack maps the one that is meaningful for its topology; the other is a gap for that pack rather than a second value to store.

apparent_power.reason: No apparent-power canonical. VA is refused into reactive_power_kvar by the cross-quantity guard, which is correct but leaves the reading unmapped.

battery_event_bitfields.reason: Model 802 battery event bitfields. inverter_event_flags is the inverter's, and a battery alarm is not an inverter alarm.

cell_index_registers.reason: Which module or string holds the extreme cell. An index, not a measurement — the voltage itself is the separate cell_level_voltage gap.

cell_level_voltage.reason: Registry has battery_cell_temp_max_c but no cell-voltage equivalent, so cell imbalance is invisible.

control_and_command_registers.reason: Write-side control, heartbeats and ramp configuration. Several are expressed as a percent of another register (InWRte is '% WChaMax'), so they are meaningless as standalone values.

dc_power.reason: DC-side power has no canonical. inverter_output_kw is the AC output; storing DC watts there would misstate inverter efficiency by the conversion loss.

meter_event_register.reason: Meter models 201-204 name their event bitfield `Evt`. The only event canonical is `inverter_event_flags`, and a meter is not an inverter — its event bits mean different things. Mapping it there would produce a field whose name asserts hardware that is not present.

model_plumbing.reason: Register-map structure, not telemetry. Correctly excluded from coverage rather than mapped to something.

nameplate_ratings.reason: Nameplate ratings and configured limits, not measurements. They describe what the equipment is, which belongs in asset metadata rather than in a telemetry field that a trend or a threshold would be computed over.

per_phase_current.reason: No per-phase canonical exists. Folding them onto line_current_a would report one phase as the total.

per_phase_measurement.reason: Per-phase variants of an aggregate the pack already maps. The registry has one field per quantity, so folding three phases onto it would report one phase as the total.

per_phase_voltage.reason: Same problem, plus line-to-line and line-to-neutral are different quantities (480 V vs 277 V on the same meter) and the registry has one voltage field.

reactive_and_apparent_energy.reason: No canonical for VAh or VArh accumulators.

reactive_and_apparent_energy_quadrants.reason: Four-quadrant VAh and VArh accumulators. No canonical for apparent or reactive energy in any quadrant.

secondary_temperatures.reason: Transformer and 'other' temperatures collide with inverter_cabinet_temp_c, which already takes TmpCab and TmpSnk.

storage_charge_status.reason: Battery charge-status enum (models 124 and 802). No canonical exists; `inverter_state` is the inverter's operating state, which is a different state machine.

storage_setpoints.reason: Model 124 control setpoints, not measurements. Several are expressed as a percent of another register (InWRte is '% WChaMax'), so they are meaningless without their referent and cannot be normalized as standalone values.

vendor_event_registers.reason: inverter_event_flags takes Evt1. The remaining bitfields are vendor-defined and would collide.
